findings.issue_text: Member add/remove routes (`delete "members"`/`put "members"`) are declared bare instead of wrapped in `member do...end`, so they don't include the `:id` param; combined with the controller calling `params.require(:group_id)` which is never supplied by the route or JS request body, every real add/remove-member request should fail with ParameterMissing or 404

Group#findMembers now defaults to `limit: 50` pagination for all groups, but the public group members template (members.hbs) was not updated with pagination controls (unlike the admin template), so groups with more than 50 members silently show only the first 50 with no way to view the rest

totalPages calculation in admin-group.js.es6 uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` instead of `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`, causing an off-by-one error when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, resulting in an extra empty page

GroupsController#members takes `limit` directly from user-controlled params with no upper bound, and the action is accessible to any user who can view the group (not admin-gated), allowing arbitrarily large queries/payloads
Admin groups controller specs call actions directly bypassing actual route definitions, so the route/param mismatch bug (missing group_id) would not be caught by the test suite
GroupsController#members response shape changed from a flat array to a wrapped object with members and meta keys, which is a breaking change for existing external API consumers

admin/groups_controller.rb add_members does `usernames.split(",")` without trimming whitespace, causing usernames with leading spaces (e.g. from "foo, bar") to fail lookup via User.find_by_username and be silently skipped
group.js findMembers, addMembers, and removeMember AJAX calls have no .catch/error handling, so failed requests fail silently with no feedback to the admin

goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Member add/remove routes (`delete "members"`/`put "members"`) are declared bare instead of wrapped in `member do...end`, so they don't include the `:id` param; combined with the controller calling `params.require(:group_id)` which is never supplied by the route or JS request body, every real add/remove-member request should fail with ParameterMissing or 404

Group#findMembers now defaults to `limit: 50` pagination for all groups, but the public group members template (members.hbs) was not updated with pagination controls (unlike the admin template), so groups with more than 50 members silently show only the first 50 with no way to view the rest

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff changes the public `/groups/:name/members` endpoint to always paginate: `GroupsController#members` now applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50)` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)` for all groups, and `Discourse.Group#findMembers` requests that JSON endpoint with `limit`/`offset` (defaulting to `limit: 50, offset: 0` on the model). In the public group members route/template, `group-members.js.es6` now sets `controller.model` to the group and calls `model.findMembers()`, and `group/members.hbs` renders `{{#each m in members}}` with no pagination controls or actions to change `offset`. Unlike the admin UI, no `next/previous` actions or links were added for the public view, so groups with >50 members will only show the first page with no way to navigate to the rest.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupsController#members takes `limit` directly from user-controlled params with no upper bound, and the action is accessible to any user who can view the group (not admin-gated), allowing arbitrarily large queries/payloads

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new code sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then applies it directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`, with no clamp/upper bound. The action is reachable by any user who passes `guardian.ensure_can_see!(group)` (i.e., not admin-only), so a client can request an arbitrarily large `limit`, producing large DB work and response payloads. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is a route/parameter key mismatch (route supplies :id but code reads :group_id), breaking the action. The candidate explicitly references this same route/param mismatch bug (missing group_id) and notes that controller specs bypass routes so the bug wouldn’t be caught. adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupsController#members response shape changed from a flat array to a wrapped object with members and meta keys, which is a breaking change for existing external API consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `GroupsController#members` from returning a flat serialized array (`render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`) to returning a wrapped JSON object with `members:` and `meta:` keys (`render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`). That is a concrete response-shape/contract change for the `/groups/:group_id/members(.json)` endpoint, and any existing clients expecting the old array JSON would break unless updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/groups_controller.rb add_members does `usernames.split(",")` without trimming whitespace, causing usernames with leading spaces (e.g. from "foo, bar") to fail lookup via User.find_by_username and be silently skipped

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff shows `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` followed by `User.find_by_username(username)`. There is no `strip`/whitespace normalization on each token, so an input like `"foo, bar"` will yield the second token as `" bar"`, causing `find_by_username` to return nil and the user to be silently skipped (the code explicitly ignores missing users). This is a concrete correctness issue in the added code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group.js findMembers, addMembers, and removeMember AJAX calls have no .catch/error handling, so failed requests fail silently with no feedback to the admin

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `findMembers`, `addMembers`, and `removeMember` return the `Discourse.ajax(...)` promise (with a `.then(...)` in some cases) but do not add an explicit `.catch(...)`. However, the finding’s claim that failures “fail silently with no feedback” is not verifiable from this diff: rejected promises may still propagate to callers (e.g., action handlers returning the promise) and `Discourse.ajax` commonly provides centralized error handling/notifications outside the shown code. The absence of a local `.catch` is therefore not a clear defect introduced by this change, and “silent failure” is speculative based on code not in the diff.
